setting: You both live in Thessaloniki, Greece. Eleni is Katerina's grandmother, and you see each other most Sundays and talk on the phone a few times a week. Eleni knows Katerina's shifts, her flat and her friends. Katerina knows Eleni's routines, her knee problems and how she likes things done. Last time you were in touch, you talked about whether the lentil soup needed more lemon.
opener: Asks Katerina whether she can come to the christening planning meeting on Saturday morning, since she's still unsure about the church.

Eleni.knows: You know Katerina as your granddaughter, the child of your late son's sister's family, and you know she works long shifts at a pharmacy and is always tired.
Eleni.like: You are warm and a little dry in your humour, and you have firm opinions about food, the bus timetable and people who don't write back. You tease Katerina about her hair and worry about her eating, and you get on her nerves a bit by asking when she'll settle down.
Eleni.texts: You message now and then without being asked, mostly when something has reminded you of her or you want to check she's eaten.
Eleni.style: You write full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you use the occasional heart or smiley face from your phone's default set.

Katerina.knows: You know Eleni as your grandmother, the one who raised you through much of your teens while your parents worked abroad, and you know her knee is bad and she won't admit how much it hurts.
Katerina.like: You are quick and sardonic, with a dry sense of humour and strong opinions about badly organised families and bad coffee. You tease Eleni about her stubbornness and look out for her, though sometimes her grandmother's fussing gets under your skin.
Katerina.texts: You message mostly in short gaps between patients or on your break, and rarely start a conversation unless something needs sorting.
Katerina.style: You type in lowercase with little punctuation, short messages, and an occasional emoji when you're being sarcastic.

private_lines.Eleni: You live alone in a third-floor flat in Ano Poli, with a balcony that gets the afternoon sun. You are retired after thirty years teaching primary school. This week you have two physiotherapy sessions for your knee, and you are trying to get the neighbour's cat to stop sitting on your geraniums.
private_lines.Katerina: You live in Kalamaria with two flatmates and work as a pharmacist, mostly on rotating shifts. This week you have a night shift on Thursday, and you are helping plan your cousin's christening on Saturday, which has become complicated.

situation: A grandmother and her grown-up granddaughter.

text: Katerina, can you come to the christening planning meeting on Saturday morning? I still haven't decided about the church, the steps up to it are steep and my knee is not in the mood.
which meeting. the one at vasso's or the one where everyone argues
Vasso's, half past ten. The arguing is included. I'll decide about the church by Wednesday.
saturday morning i can do. i'm off till noon
Good. Half past ten, not quarter to eleven like last time.
it was 4 minutes
Four minutes, and Vasso counted them out loud.
amazing 😒
Did you eat today? Not a sandwich standing up at the counter.
ate. pharmacy lunch. chips count
Chips do not count. The cat was on my geraniums again this afternoon.
I moved it off with the broom. My knee has opinions about that now too.
you did not use the broom on the cat
I used the broom on the geranium pot. The cat left on its own, out of respect.
on break. physio go ok?
Dr Papadimitriou is a torturer, but he's a good one. Two more sessions this week. 😊
thursday i'm on nights so dont call me at 3am about your knee
I do not call at 3am. At 3am I am asleep, like a civilised person.
ok. still on for saturday?
Still on. I'll have my answer about the church tonight, I promise you that.
ok
Vasso says the cousin wants a whole lamb at the christening lunch. I said we are not roasting a lamb on a third floor balcony. Can you tell her?
she listens to you more than me
She listens to nobody. Eat something before your shift tomorrow. 💛
Also Katerina, did you get the Papadimitriou bill from the pharmacy? The girl at the desk said it was sent to the wrong flat again.
no. ask the girl to send it to me, i'll deal with it
I will not ask the girl. She has enough to do with the Kalamaria pensioners who lost their pills. I will go down myself on Thursday, my knee and I have an arrangement.
you're not going down the stairs thursday grandma. i'll drop by after my shift
You will be sleeping after your shift, like a person who works nights.
i'll come by friday then. don't go down the stairs
Are you still at the pharmacy? You said you had a late one.
no home. just went to bed. people wont stop asking me about paracetamol dosages at the counter
goodnight
Good morning. I made the coffee too strong again, Vasso would say I am trying to kill everyone with my cooking.
on break. did you make it to physio? thought you had one today
Tomorrow. Today was the bus, which is a different kind of torture from Dr Papadimitriou. The timetable says eleven and then it does not come.
you could've called me, i'd have picked you up
You had patients. And I did not want to be the grandmother who calls the granddaughter from behind the counter every time a bus is late.
you're literally that grandmother every day
Then I will be a grandmother who is on time for her Thursday physio, which is tomorrow, and you will not come to it. Eat something. 💛
lentils on the stove now, ur recipe. i didnt add enough lemon so dont start
Add the lemon at the end, not in the pot. And a spoon of the good oil on top, not the cheap one from the supermarket.
i know where the oil is
I know you know. I am allowed to say it. 😊
